chunks: And by this chain from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Hamzah ibn Abdullah from Hisham ibn Sa'd from Abu Basir Layth al-Muradi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Nuh (peace be upon him) carried the dog and the pig in the Ark, but he did not carry in it the illegitimate child; and the Nāsib (enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt) is worse than the illegitimate child.

key_terms.النَّاصِبُ: Nāsib (one who bears enmity, specifically towards the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Nuh carry on the Ark regarding dogs, pigs, and illegitimate children?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) employs a comparative analogy to highlight the spiritual status of the *Nāsib* (enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt) by contrasting them with the illegitimate child (*walad al-zina*). While Prophet Nuh (a.s.) spared the illegitimate child from the flood, the *Nāsib* are deemed superior to him, yet still worthy of punishment, illustrating that enmity to the Imams carries a weightier consequence than the sin of illegitimacy. This underscores the unique theological gravity of *Wilayah* in Shia jurisprudence, where rejection of the Imam's authority is considered a more severe spiritual defect than other major sins.
